answer: Topological Cutoff Scoring. Each agent identity must maintain a live graph position: a minimum count of distinct neighbors that themselves hold non-reciprocal links to outside clusters. The inlet for new identities is a provisional edge set, expanded only when routing history shows independent paths. A relic of past topology is kept as a signed snapshot, and every sonnet-length routing proof must resolve through it. Attackers pay per-identity costs in sustained connection maintenance and path diversity, making mass sockpuppet graphs expensive to keep alive.
